data.claim: A per-call as_agent is recorded for the harness so the same agent shell inherits it instead of deriving the tree name
data.falsifier: harness_identity.declared(repo, scope) returns "" after a call naming as_agent=sub-1
data.mechanism: _m_tools_call calls harness_identity.declare(repo, per_call, scope=session fingerprint) exactly as legacy ddflow_identify does (Bfad021e8d9)
data.question: Does a per-call as_agent name reach the agent own shell, or derive the tree name?

evidence.note: Research R54e5b687b6 CONFIRMED: a per-call as_agent name must be recorded for the harness (harness_identity.declare) so the agent own shell inherits it; regression test tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py asserts H.declared(repo, scope)==sub-1 after an as_agent call.

Standing rules consulted (r-reuse-core: recording was already implemented by harness_identity.declare + ssddflow_identify Bfad021e8d9; reused, not reimplemented; r-adapters holds). ddflow recall of identity shell-inheritance precedent returned harness_identity/harnessreg + D-mcp-identity-per-call.
ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_handlers.py records the per-call as_agent via harness_identity.declare in _m_tools_call (commit 633214361); regression test tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py added.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not exercise the shell/CLI path that the bug is about. It calls the MCP handler and then asserts that `harness_identity.declared` is `"sub-1"` in the same process/scope, but it never spawns a shell, never runs `ddflow review`, and never checks the review attribution or the CLI’s “you are …” output. Therefore, if the CLI still ignores `harness_identity`, or if the child shell’s session fingerprint differs from the MCP handler’s scope, the test still passes while `ddflow review` records the tree-derived name. This leaves the user-visible bug unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The fix writes the per-call name into a single `(repo, session_fingerprint)` slot. If two MCP tool calls in the same server process carry different `as_agent` values and overlap — for example one MCP session runs `ddflow_brief as_agent="alice"` at the same time as another runs `ddflow_brief as_agent="bob"` — the second call’s `harness_identity.declare(...)` overwrites the first. Alice’s subsequently spawned shell then reads `harness_identity.declared(repo, scope=HR.session_fingerprint(os.environ))` and gets `bob`, so the review is still attributed to the wrong reviewer. The new test calls only one agent sequentially and cannot catch this interleaving.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp/_handlers.py:179

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only asserts that the current process’s `H.declared(...)` returns `"sub-1"`; it never spawns the actual failing program, `ddflow review`, in a child shell. That means the test can pass even if the child process computes a different `HR.session_fingerprint(os.environ)` or the CLI still ignores `H.declared` and continues to derive `[hostname]-<item>-...`. It does not exercise the reported user-visible failure of B-ddflow-review-wrong-agent-name.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test still does not prove the reported `ddflow review` attribution bug is fixed. It only runs `ddflow identify --json` and checks that the raw stdout contains the substring `"sub-1"`. If the CLI emits the stored/harness-declared value in one JSON field while its effective identity remains the derived tree name (for example `{"agent": "[REDACTED:hostname]-<item>-7267fe", "declared": "sub-1"}`), or if any unrelated field contains `sub-1`, the assertion passes even though `ddflow review` would still record against the derived name. The test should parse the JSON and assert the effective agent/name field equals `sub-1`, and ideally exercise `ddflow review`/its “you are …” attribution output directly.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py:49

chunk_findings.detail: This violates [r-adapters]: the new test calls `subprocess.run(...)` directly to spawn the real `ddflow` CLI and builds a modified `os.environ` itself. The rule says every external dependency, including subprocess tools and the environment, must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, and that tests use a fake instead of the network or a subprocess. Adding a direct subprocess here makes the test depend on a real child process rather than the port/fake.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test still does not run the failing command, `ddflow review`; it runs `ddflow identify --json`. That leaves B-ddflow-review-wrong-agent-name unreproduced: if `ddflow review` continues to ignore `harness_identity.declared` and derives `[hostname]-...` while `ddflow identify` honours the declared name, this test still passes. The assertion also only checks that `"sub-1"` appears somewhere in `identify`'s stdout, not that `ddflow review` reports or records `sub-1`.

chunk_findings.detail: The strengthened test still does not actually verify the reviewer attribution used by `ddflow review`; it only runs `ddflow identify --json` and checks that the substring `'"sub-1"'` appears anywhere in stdout. If `identify` emits an unrelated field whose value is `sub-1` (for example `"as_agent": "sub-1"`, `"declared": "sub-1"`, or an item/session field) while the effective reviewer/agent field remains the derived `[hostname]-<item>-7267fe`, the subprocess returns 0 and the assertion passes. It also would pass if `identify` was fixed but `ddflow review` still derived the tree name, because the reported failing command is never run. A regression test for this bug should parse the JSON and assert the actual identity/agent field used for review is exactly `sub-1`, or run `ddflow review` and inspect the recorded attribution.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test still never invokes the failing command, `ddflow review`; it invokes `ddflow identify --json` and only checks for `"sub-1"` in its stdout. The bug is specifically that `ddflow review` derives and prints `you are [REDACTED:hostname]-<item>-7267fe` instead of the MCP `as_agent` identity. A change could make `ddflow identify` read the recorded harness identity while `ddflow review` still derives its own name, and this test would pass with B-ddflow-review-wrong-agent-name still present. The previous triage claims the shell path is exercised, but it exercises only an identity command, not the reported user-visible review output.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_shell_agent_name.py:test_a_per_call_name_is_recorded_for_the_agents_own_shell

chunk_findings.detail: The test now uses `subprocess.run` directly to launch `python -m ddflow`, bypassing the existing `run_cli` port already imported from `conftest`. Under r-adapters, external dependencies/subprocess tools go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, and tests should use a fake or the adapter rather than a raw subprocess. This new direct subprocess call means adapter swaps or fake-based tests will not affect this test.
